1. Resetting the chilled water temperature setpoint from 7°C to 9°C between 11:00 hrs and 15:00 hrs on weekdays.

3. Reducing the fresh air damper opening from 30% to 20% during the solar peak window, subject to CO2 sensor readings remaining within acceptable limits.

We estimate that this change could reduce grid energy consumption by approximately 8–10% during the peak solar hours. However, since this involves a modification to the BMS setpoints, we require your formal approval before implementation.

We are aware that the BMS software upgrade is scheduled for 12-04-2025. We would like to submit this change request before the upgrade so that the new control logic can be incorporated during the upgrade itself, if approved.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The annual energy audit of M/s GreenTech Commercial Complex was conducted on 20 March 2025. The facility is a mixed-use commercial building comprising office floors, a retail podium, and a dedicated data centre on the lower ground floor. The total connected load is 1,850 kW with a contract demand of 1,200 kVA.

The total electrical energy consumption during the audit period (April 2024 – March 2025) was 3,915,480 kWh. The maximum demand recorded during the year was 482.5 kW, which occurred on 12 June 2024 between 14:00 and 15:00 hrs. This value is the current recorded peak for the facility and replaces the earlier historical peak of 480.5 kW that had been recorded on 21 May 2023. The new peak demand of 482.5 kW will be referenced for all future tariff computations and demand-side management planning.

The specific energy consumption (SEC) for the facility is 12.8 kWh/sq.m/month, which is 7% higher than the benchmark of 12.0 kWh/sq.m/month for similar commercial complexes in the region. The power factor has remained above 0.93 throughout the audit period, with an average of 0.95.

Key observations include condenser fouling in two of the three chillers, suboptimal set-points for the precision cooling units in the data centre, and the continued operation of legacy fluorescent fittings in basement parking areas. Recommendations to address these issues are detailed in Section 7.

---

2. AUDIT METHODOLOGY

The audit was carried out as per the MEDA Energy Audit Manual (Rev. 4, 2023) and in accordance with IS 15369:2003. The methodology comprised:

- Review of previous audit reports (2023 and 2024)

- Power quality analyser (Fluke 435-II) connected at the main LT panel for 7 days to capture load profiles
- Thermal imaging of switchgear and distribution panels
- Ultrasonic flow meter measurements on chilled water circuits

- Temperature and humidity logging in the data centre (7-day continuous)

2.3 Data Analysis
- Normalisation of consumption data for weather variations using degree-day method
- Comparison of measured performance with design values and industry benchmarks
- Regression analysis of monthly consumption against production/non-production variables

All instruments used were calibrated within the last 12 months. The overall measurement uncertainty is estimated at ±2.5% for energy measurements and ±3.0% for thermal measurements.
